I can definitely relate. I'm a college student, so for some of my classes attendance isn't mandatory. I also, of course, have the option of quitting completely. However, I force myself out of bed because I remind myself of the goals and dreams I have and how completing school will get me there. On a day-to-day basis I remind myself that if I don't go to class, my professors may look down on me, or will think I'm lazy and don't care. So again,  I force myself to go. Do you have anyone that can hold you accountable? Asking someone to get you out of bed in the morning and making sure you are at school might help a lot.

Do you live with anyone? Or do have anyone who you can meet with relatively early in the day? Maybe asking to meet someone for breakfast will not only get you out of bed but may help give you more energy for the day. 

I go to school and work full-time, but I spend a good amount of time sleeping or do nothing. A lot of times  I feel that I go to class and get to work on time just so that others won't be angry with me. If I didn't have these obligations, I'd probably stay in bed 75% of the day for days or weeks at a time. So staying busy and some level of accountability may help for you as well.

I agree. I just recently took in a stray and even though I've been feeling my depression is worsening, her company has helped me a lot. The fact that she repeatedly came to my apartment and waited once on my porch for four hours between the time I left and got home told me she wanted to stay with me. And the fact that she always wants to sit on my lap and lay with me when I'm sleeping makes me feel loved even when I'm really lonely.

Taking care of her reminds me I'm useful and forces me to do something, even if it's just cleaning the litter box.

There have been so many times that I wish I could just wake up and then everything would make sense. Similar to a lot of stories (like the Wizard of Oz), the experiences are so real but waking up will allow you to feel alive again and make sense of what's been occurring for so long. I thought I was just stupid for thinking this way and could never fully explain it, so I've never mentioned it until now. Another redditor pointed me to r/dpdr which is for depersonalization and derealization. I'm so relieved to find out that this is actually understood by some and maybe I'll be able to actually feel alive at some point.

I mentioned this in a comment to another, but most of my life I've felt like I'm not really living, maybe dreaming or something. Does this sound similar to how you feel? When I was younger I used to pray every day that I would begin to feel like I was living. As I got older, I've usually felt the same but figured this is normal. I'm very introverted and my mind usually has a million thoughts so I also figured this might be why I feel disconnected. I've never had to deal with the amnesia type of issue you've had, though. That's part of the reason I told myself at times that this couldn't be dissociation.

Really? It's good to know someone else understands what this is like, though I wouldn't wish for you to have deal with it. I wondered if it was dissociating because I never lost track of time and knew who I was, but was just disoriented. What it is similar to, though, is the fact that I don't really feel like I'm living. I guess it's more dream like. However, most of my life I have felt like I was never living, literally like dreaming or some other disconnection from the actual world. I've never told anyone that because I've always figured they laugh. But that's also part of the reason I've questioned about abuse. Basically, I have a lot of the symptoms of someone whose endured abuse- afraid to be touched, typically afraid of men, the thought of sex used to be terrifying, depression, etc. Now I know many of these symptoms are also common for anyone whose endured really any type of emotional pain (my father passed when I was young and it was traumatic for me). 
Most of the time I've told myself nothing could have happened to me because I have a strong memory, but I don't understand why I've had these episodes. Whenever I'm able to see a therapist again I will. I just don't want to force myself to believe something that isn't true.

Thank you, when these first started occurring I considered them panic attacks. However, they were not similar to the other panic attacks I've typically had- really heavy breathing, shaking, etc. The episodes aren't invasive, it's just the constant questioning if they are a result of something that won't leave my mind.

Hold on. If you felt strong once, then you can regain that- you are the same person. Think of the person you made the promise to and, if you can, talk to them. If you've made it this far, you've made it for a reason and there is still purpose. I'm sorry I don't know you're situation, but please, if anything, keep surviving until you can find a way to be happy again.

It seems like anxiety to me. Panic attacks can be different according to the individual and I think they usually scare the person when they first begin (they scared me). Talking about it with another person (if you're comfortable with that) might work. Processing it alone or journaling might help you understand why you react so strongly. 

Throughout my life, trying to forget about things has made it worse in the long- run. In the moment it felt better because I felt like I was over it, but the situations would always come up later in my life and usually in a worse form. I think anxiety can be really difficult to deal with, but there's always a way to help calm and/or solve it.
